items.stem: The work-energy principle states that the net work done on a body equals:

options.text: The change in its kinetic energy
options.rationale: Correct: net work = change in kinetic energy.
Weight is a force, not energy.
Impulse relates to momentum, not the work-energy principle.
Momentum is mass times velocity, not work.

items.explanation: Correct: net work = change in kinetic energy.

items.stem: Which TWO are true for a perfectly inelastic collision? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: momentum is conserved in collisions with no external impulse.

options.text: The bodies move together after impact
options.rationale: Correct: perfectly inelastic means they stick and share a velocity.
That describes an elastic, not inelastic, collision.

items.explanation: Correct: momentum is conserved in collisions with no external impulse.

items.stem: For a wheel rolling without slipping, the contact point:

options.text: Has zero instantaneous velocity relative to the ground
options.rationale: Correct: rolling without slipping means no relative sliding at the contact.

options.text: Moves fastest of all points on the wheel
options.rationale: The contact point is instantaneously at rest, the slowest.

options.text: Moves at the same speed as the centre
options.rationale: The top moves at twice the centre's speed, not the contact.
A normal force still acts at the contact.

items.explanation: Correct: rolling without slipping means no relative sliding at the contact.
